reason: The hypothesis directly restates the deformation mechanism transition (dislocation slip to twinning) and its effects on mechanical properties as reported in P28 for Al0.3CoCrFeNi, and applies it to FeNiCrMn without new mechanistic insight or integration of conflicting evidence. The idea that low SFE promotes twinning and hardening is well-established in the literature (P3, P15, P34) and is simply transferred to a new composition without justification.

low stacking fault energy promotes twinning
twins act as barriers to dislocation motion and enhance strain hardening
increased twin density and higher yield strength/strain hardening at cryogenic/high strain rates
dislocation slip predominates at ambient/low strain rates
